profiles.name: Kai lan
profiles.overview: Kai lan is a leafy brassica in the Alboglabra group; its leaves and stems are used as vegetables.
profiles.conditions: NParks describes full sun, well-drained soil and moderate watering. This is Singapore gardening guidance, not a field-specific irrigation schedule.
profiles.water: NParks describes moderate watering for kai lan. That qualitative gardening guidance does not give an irrigation volume for your farm.
profiles.harvest: NParks gives 21–55 days to harvest. Cultivar, establishment method and local conditions affect timing; this is a reference range, not a harvest prediction.
profiles.rotation: As a brassica, kai lan shares a crop-family group with crops such as radish. A family change can be one rotation consideration; local pest history and a suitable break period are still needed.
profiles.limitation: Kai lan is available as sourced knowledge, but it has not been added to the validated rotation-screening catalog.

profiles.name: Rice
profiles.referenceScope: The IRRI reference describes establishment practices; it does not provide a planting calendar for every country.
profiles.overview: Rice can be established by direct seeding or transplanting. IRRI explains that planting time depends on the locality, variety, water availability and intended harvest time.
profiles.conditions: For rice, check the local variety, water availability and establishment method together. IRRI describes a prepared seedbed for establishment; a country name alone cannot establish a suitable planting date.
profiles.water: Rice water management depends on the production system, establishment method and local water supply. The saved IRRI reference does not establish an irrigation amount for your field.
profiles.harvest: Rice harvest timing depends on the variety, locality and establishment method. I do not have a verified maturity duration for your local variety.

profiles.name: Wheat
profiles.referenceScope: The cultivation reference describes Minnesota spring wheat; its calendar is not validated for other regions or wheat types.
profiles.overview: Wheat has spring and winter growth types. Their response to cold differs, so the wheat type matters before discussing planting dates.
profiles.conditions: Winter wheat needs a period of cold for normal development; spring wheat does not have the same cold requirement. Select a locally adapted type before applying a planting calendar.
profiles.harvest: Wheat maturity varies by variety and season. The Minnesota reference timeline cannot be used as a harvest prediction for another region.

profiles.name: Tomato
profiles.referenceScope: The cultivation reference is Minnesota home-garden guidance; local varieties and planting dates remain unverified.
profiles.overview: Tomatoes are warm-season, sun-loving plants. Bush and vining types differ in growth habit and harvest pattern.
profiles.conditions: UMN describes full sun and a frost-free growing period, with transplants set out after the soil warms. This is a general reference, not a local planting date.
profiles.harvest: Bush tomatoes tend to ripen over a concentrated period; vining types continue flowering and fruiting while conditions permit. A local variety is needed to discuss days to harvest.
profiles.rotation: Tomatoes share a family group with potatoes, peppers and eggplants. The UMN gardening guide recommends rotating away from these related crops; the required local break still depends on pest history.
